text:
oliver: quick bring-up notes for nebula-11b-int6 vs baseline 13b-fp16 on GTN customer slice. short thread.

maya: thanks — quick TL;DR?

oliver: TL;DR: ~30% unit-cost reduction for common chat flows, better tail latency, small quality hit on long-form reasoning. details below.

sam: numbers pls.

oliver: Eval run details:
- sample: 2k mixed-turn chat + 500 rerank pairs (customer slice B)
- command: ./eval_tool --model nebula-11b-int6 --baseline 13b-fp16 --slice customerB --samples 2500 --save-disagreements --output s3://evals/nebula-int6/3312345679/

Observed metrics:
- unit econ: int6 ~ $0.27 / 1k tokens vs 13b-fp16 ~ $0.39 / 1k tokens (~30.8% savings)
- latency: int6 p50=48ms p95=130ms; 13b p50=68ms p95=185ms
- quality: primary metric exact-answer F1 -> int6 -1.2pp vs 13b (dialogue QA); rerank NDCG -0.4pp
- error rate: 0.02% increase in model errors (tokenization mismatch)

nina: where does the quality hit show up most?

oliver: slice breakdown:
- short Qs (<200 tokens): parity or slight win for int6 (fewer hallucinations on simple prompts)
- multi-hop reasoning and long-context (>800 tokens): int6 degrades, divergence increases with prompt length
- rerank: negligible UX impact for baseline ranking endpoints

maya: product recommendation?

oliver: proposed routing and defaults:
1) Default nebula-int6 for: short conversational read-only endpoints, embeddings, high-volume rerank endpoints.
2) Keep 13b-fp16 for: code-editors, long-form compose, and multi-step reasoning endpoints.
3) Routing rule: if prompt_length > 600 OR complexity_score >= 0.65 -> send to 13b, otherwise nebula-int6.

sam: rollout plan? canary thresholds?

oliver: rollout draft:
- 5% traffic for 48h, capture online diffs + top-100 disagreements to S3.
- Guard rails to expand:
  * no regression > 1.5pp on exact-answer F1 for canary slice
  * p95 latency within SLO + 60ms
  * error rate delta < 0.15% absolute
- Immediate rollback trigger: >2.0pp regression OR critical customer reports

nina: ops notes?

oliver: ops checklist:
- add warmup hook: run synthetic warmup prompts on any new int6 pod to prime KV cache.
- autoscaler: reduce min replicas for int6 pool by 1 to cut standing cost; monitor tail latency closely.
- tracing: attach eval_tag=nebula-int6 to canary requests and enable disagreement capture.

maya: EvalBot, auto checks?

EvalBot: regression-checker: observed delta -1.2pp (threshold 1.5pp). ALERT=FALSE but recommends manual review of top-100 disagreements. Scheduled follow-up perf run in 24h to collect more tail samples.

sam: capture examples in ops dashboard and product team should review top disagreements before 20% rollout.

oliver: agreed. I'll open PR with routing rule, canary config, warmup hook, and attach CSV of per-slice metrics. Link will be posted here when ready.

maya: I'll draft GTN blurb: "~30% cost reduction for short conversational flows with near-parity UX; keep long-form editors on 13b." Will include rollout steps and rollback criteria.

nina: one more ask  can we instrument complexity_score on client side for a smooth routing signal?

oliver: yes, suggest complexity_score computed server-side during request preproc (cheap heuristics) and exposed to routing service. I'll include the proposal in the PR.

sam: :thumbsup: ping when canary starts.

EvalBot: note logged: follow-up run scheduled + disagreement archive at s3://evals/nebula-int6/3312345679/disagreements.json

oliver: thanks all. conservative rollout.
